- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the following 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline from peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% per day of reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “sentiment-weighted decay” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for days with high sentiment volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift from positive to negative (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in the next 3–5 days.
